versions.label: Earlier
versions.summary: Two 46-storey residential towers and a two-storey non-residential building are proposed at Labatt Avenue and River Street. Pickup ends at 6 p.m., deliveries can start at 6 a.m., and the pedestrian route crosses the loading access.
arrangements: Accessible passenger pickup at the main entrance is available until 6 p.m.
Routine commercial deliveries can begin at 6 a.m.
The proposed pedestrian route crosses the loading access.
The proposal includes two 46-storey residential towers and a two-storey non-residential building.

features.title: Accessible pickup
features.prompt: How do you feel about the main entrance pickup bay closing at 6 p.m.?

features.title: Delivery hours
features.prompt: How do you feel about routine commercial deliveries starting at 6 a.m.?

features.title: Pedestrian access
features.prompt: How do you feel about the pedestrian route crossing the loading access?

features.title: Building height and scale
features.prompt: How do you feel about the proposed 46-storey towers?

responses.comment: My Wheel-Trans ride often arrives after dinner. I can wait inside the main entrance until it comes. I’d support the plan if I could still get picked up there at 8 p.m.

condition.requirement: Keep accessible pickup available at the main entrance until at least 8 p.m.

assessment.explanation: The 9 p.m. closing time covers the requested 8 p.m. pickup at the main entrance.

responses.comment: My bedroom faces the loading entrance. I already hear trucks backing up from the other side of the block. Six is too early.

condition.requirement: Start routine commercial deliveries at 9 a.m. or later so nearby residents can sleep.

assessment.explanation: The routine delivery window now begins at 9 a.m.

responses.comment: I pass through with a stroller most mornings. I don’t want to stop in a truck driveway while a driver is checking both mirrors.

condition.requirement: Provide a step-free pedestrian route that bypasses the loading driveway.

assessment.explanation: The separate step-free route bypasses the loading access.

responses.comment: We get a bakery order at 7:30 before the first rush. The driver serves three other shops on the same run. Please keep the early slot available.

condition.requirement: Allow bakery deliveries around 7:30 a.m.

assessment.explanation: The new routine delivery window starts after the bakery’s requested slot.

responses.comment: A better driveway wouldn’t make two 46-storey towers feel right here. I’d like to see shorter buildings.

condition.requirement: Reduce the height of both residential towers.

responses.comment: I support adding homes here.
My visits are usually midday. I’d like to see a proper site plan before I decide.
Six in the morning? Please move that later. I work evenings and I’m barely asleep by two.

condition.requirement: Keep routine loading quiet until at least 9 a.m. for neighbours who work late.

assessment.explanation: The routine delivery window starts at 9 a.m.

responses.comment: My dad comes for dinner on Thursdays. His ride home usually comes around quarter to eight. Please keep pickup by the lobby open that late.

condition.requirement: Keep the main entrance pickup bay available around 7:45 p.m. for evening visitors who need accessible rides.

assessment.explanation: The revised pickup hours cover 7:45 p.m. at the main entrance.

responses.comment: I could support it if the kids had a way to walk past without crossing the truck entrance.

condition.requirement: Give children walking past the site a pedestrian route clear of loading traffic.

assessment.explanation: The separate pedestrian route avoids the loading access.

responses.comment: Happy to have more people nearby, less happy about delivery trucks starting up while we’re still setting up.
The bay closing at six is the part that sticks out. Evening pickup would be useful.

condition.requirement: Keep accessible pickup available into the evening.

assessment.explanation: The main entrance pickup now runs until 9 p.m.

responses.comment: Forty-six floors is too much at this corner. Bring both buildings down.

condition.requirement: Lower both residential towers.

assessment.explanation: The tower heights stay at 46 storeys.

responses.comment: A lift after my physio appointment can take ages. I need a place near the door, even if it’s raining and my ride is late.

condition.requirement: Provide covered waiting beside the main entrance pickup bay.

assessment.explanation: The revised hours give more time to wait. The passage leaves shelter unspecified.

responses.comment: A truck crossing there is awkward enough on a normal day. When the sidewalk is iced over you can’t exactly step aside quickly.

condition.requirement: Route pedestrians away from the loading driveway.

assessment.explanation: The pedestrian route is now separate from the loading access.

responses.comment: More homes are welcome. The early trucks and the shared crossing are what would make it hard for me to live with.
I’m for the new homes. I would still move the truck start to nine.

condition.requirement: Start routine commercial deliveries at 9 a.m. or later.

assessment.explanation: Routine commercial deliveries now start at 9 a.m.

responses.comment: Good spot for more apartments.
I’m fine with the height. That driveway crossing looks fiddly.
Is that delivery start time for our suppliers too, or just the new businesses?
Can we see a shadow study for the houses along River before going any further?

condition.requirement: Publish a shadow study for homes along River Street.

assessment.explanation: The height passage describes the same towers and leaves shadow impacts open.

responses.comment: I only cut through here once a week. The crossing seems like something to fix.

versions.label: Current
versions.summary: The revision keeps both 46-storey towers and the two-storey building. It extends accessible pickup, delays routine deliveries, and provides a separate step-free pedestrian route.
arrangements: Accessible passenger pickup at the main entrance is available until 9 p.m.
Routine commercial deliveries are scheduled from 9 to 11 a.m.
A separate step-free pedestrian route avoids the loading access.
The proposal includes two 46-storey residential towers and a two-storey non-residential building.

responses.comment: The separate path makes a big difference with the stroller. Will it get cleared after a snowfall?

condition.requirement: Clear snow from the separate step-free route so it stays passable with strollers.

responses.comment: Nine to eleven misses our bakery drop and overlaps with the lunch prep. Could we book one earlier slot?

condition.requirement: Allow a bookable 7:30 a.m. bakery delivery slot.

responses.comment: The access changes are good. I’m still against the scale. Two towers at 46 storeys is too high here.

condition.requirement: Reduce the height of both residential towers.

responses.comment: I support adding homes here.
My visits are usually midday. I’d like to see a proper site plan before I decide.
Much better. Nine gives me a few more hours of quiet. Do the same hours apply Saturday?

condition.requirement: Confirm that the 9 a.m. delivery start applies on weekends.

responses.comment: That covers Dad’s ride home. I’m glad pickup is still right by the lobby.
I’m happy with the separate path. That’s the bit I was waiting to see.
We can work with the hours if drivers know where to wait. Please post the hours by the bay.

condition.requirement: Post delivery hours where drivers can read them from the loading bay.

responses.comment: Nine works much better for dinner visits. I still find the towers a bit much.
Later trucks are a relief. I still want both towers brought down.

condition.requirement: Lower both residential towers.

responses.comment: That would cover my ride after physio. I’d still like a dry place to wait by the door.

condition.requirement: Provide covered waiting beside the main entrance pickup bay.

responses.comment: I’m on board now that the path skips the driveway. Please keep it clear all winter.

condition.requirement: Maintain a clear step-free path through winter.

responses.comment: The later start and the path were the two things I worried about. This version works for me.
Yes to the homes, and yes to the later start.
Good spot for more apartments. Staying until nine for pickup helps, too.
The path fixes my main sticking point.
Still working out whether our suppliers can fit their runs into that window.
I like the access changes. I’d support the plan if the two towers were shorter.

condition.requirement: Reduce the proposed height of both towers.

responses.comment: I can visit my sister after work and still book a ride from the main doors.
Where does the step-free path meet the public sidewalk? It’s hard to tell from this description.

condition.requirement: Show where the step-free route connects to the public sidewalk.

building-scale.label: Reduce the height of the towers

step-free-route-details.label: Keep the step-free route usable in winter
